claim: CKAMP39, CKAMP52, and CKAMP59, together with CKAMP44, constitute a novel family of auxiliary subunits distinct from other families of AMPAR interacting proteins.
source: Here, we report on three AMPAR interacting proteins—namely CKAMP39, CKAMP52 and CKAMP59—that, together with the previously characterized CKAMP44, constitute a novel family of auxiliary subunits distinct from other families of AMPAR interacting proteins.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by structural analysis, phylogenetic analysis, and functional characterization presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The new members of the CKAMP family display distinct regional and developmental expression profiles in the mouse brain.
source: The new members of the CKAMP family display distinct regional and developmental expression profiles in the mouse brain.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2A and BioGPS database analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: CKAMP family members exert diverse modulation on AMPAR gating by influencing deactivation, desensitization and recovery from desensitization.
source: Notably, despite their structural similarities they exert diverse modulation on AMPAR gating by influencing deactivation, desensitization and recovery from desensitization, as well as glutamate and cyclothiazide potency to AMPARs.
evidence: Supported by electrophysiological recordings in Xenopus oocytes (Figure 3) and HEK293/T17 cells (Figure 5).

claim: CKAMP family members influence glutamate and cyclothiazide potency to AMPARs.
source: Notably, despite their structural similarities they exert diverse modulation on AMPAR gating by influencing deactivation, desensitization and recovery from desensitization, as well as glutamate and cyclothiazide potency to AMPARs.
evidence: Supported by dose-response experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: AMPAR function is very precisely controlled by the cell-type specific expression of the CKAMP family members.
source: This study indicates that AMPAR function is very precisely controlled by the cell-type specific expression of the CKAMP family members.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combination of distinct expression patterns and diverse functional effects of CKAMP family members.

claim: Cystine-knot containing proteins differ much in their function.
